title: Sky's website IP must be transferred to a Dai-Foundation-like entity rather than held by an operator
content:
A.5.1.1.1 states the IP rights of the Sky website must be transferred to an entity similar to the Dai Foundation.

The comparison is the operative detail: that body exists to hold trademarks and assets neutrally rather than to operate products. Applying the pattern separates **custody** of the brand from **operation** of the frontend, so an operator losing funding or mandate cannot put the domain or trademark at risk.

This is the accessibility-side counterpart to holding protocol contracts immutably — the user-facing entry point gets its own custody guarantee, because a domain is a single point of failure that no amount of on-chain immutability protects.
description: A.5.1.1.1 puts the brand's core asset in a neutral custodian, separating trademark and domain custody from whoever operates the frontend day to day.
